description: Na₃BP₂O₈ crystallizes in the monoclinic C2/c space group. There are four inequivalent Na sites. In the first Na site, Na is bonded in a 7-coordinate geometry to seven O atoms. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.32-2.65 Å. In the second Na site, Na is bonded in a 6-coordinate geometry to six O atoms. There are two shorter (2.28 Å) and four longer (2.49 Å) Na-O bond lengths. In the third Na site, Na is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to four O atoms. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.31-2.48 Å. In the fourth Na site, Na is bonded in a 8-coordinate geometry to eight O atoms. There are a spread of Na-O bond distances ranging from 2.40-2.93 Å. B is bonded to four O atoms to form BO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with four PO₄ tetrahedra. There are three shorter (1.48 Å) and one longer (1.51 Å) B-O bond length. There are two inequivalent P sites. In the first P site, P is bonded to four O atoms to form PO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with two equivalent BO₄ tetrahedra. There are a spread of P-O bond distances ranging from 1.51-1.61 Å. In the second P site, P is bonded to four O atoms to form PO₄ tetrahedra that share corners with two equivalent BO₄ tetrahedra. There are a spread of P-O bond distances ranging from 1.52-1.60 Å. There are eight inequivalent O sites. In the first O site, O is bonded to three Na and one P atom to form distorted corner-sharing ONa₃P tetrahedra. In the second O site, O is bonded in a 2-coordinate geometry to two Na, one B, and one P atom. In the third O site, O is bonded in a distorted rectangular see-saw-like geometry to three Na and one P atom. In the fourth O site, O is bonded in a 3-coordinate geometry to one Na, one B, and one P atom. In the fifth O site, O is bonded in a 5-coordinate geometry to four Na and one P atom. In the sixth O site, O is bonded in a 3-coordinate geometry to two Na and one P atom. In the seventh O site, O is bonded in a distorted bent 120 degrees geometry to one Na, one B, and one P atom. In the eighth O site, O is bonded in a 4-coordinate geometry to two Na, one B, and one P atom.
